answer:
Apple's Greater China net sales fell from $66.95 billion in FY2024 to $64.38 billion in FY2025, a decline of $2.58 billion (−3.8%, shown as (4)% in the 10-K), and yes — the FY2025 10-K explains the decrease.

- **FY2024 (ended September 28, 2024):** $66.95 billion; **FY2025 (ended September 27, 2025):** $64.38 billion — a decrease of $2.58 billion, or −3.8%.
- **Why (per the 10-K):** "Greater China net sales decreased during 2025 compared to 2024 primarily due to lower net sales of iPhone, partially offset by higher net sales of Mac" (Item 7, MD&A, Segment Operating Performance).
- This was the second consecutive annual decline in the segment: Greater China was $72.56 billion in FY2023, down 8% in FY2024 and another 4% in FY2025, even as Apple's total net sales grew 6% to $416.2 billion in FY2025.
- Note: Greater China is one of Apple's five reportable segments (its reportable segments are geographic, not product-based).

Sources:
- [SQL: geographic_revenue]
- [AAPL FY2025 10-K, p.24] (MD&A, Segment Operating Performance / Greater China)
- [AAPL FY2025 10-K, p.48] (Note 13 – Segment Information and Geographic Data)
